newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 to 2.00 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 to 2.00 lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents per lb lower on Wednesday, after a disappointing performance in London overnight, traders said.

Traders said the London market's failure to make its $40-$60 higher due weighed on sentiment. Robusta futures were firmer early Wednesday in thin trade. At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was up $25, to $1,840, the session high.

Tuesday, New York arabica futures ended mixed in sluggish dealings. September fell 0.35 cent per lb, to 175.10, after ranging from 179.00 to 171.75. Spot July finished 3.35 cents higher, at 198.00, while the outer months closed up 0.20 to down 3.40.
The July/September switch widened to 22.90 cents, from 19.45 cents at the close on Monday.

Technically, traders pegged near-term September support at 172.00 cents, with major support seen at 168.75 cents, a low reached last week. On the upside, September near-term resistance was put at 180.00 cents, followed by 185.00 cents.

On the weather front, no damaging cold is expected in the next several days in Brazil's coffee belt, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday. Low temperatures are forecast at 54-63 F, it said.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 250 60-kg bags as of June 23, to 46,175 bags. There were 9,512 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
